---
title: "Examples from the help file"
subtitle: "The examples at the end of help mecompare, run in full"
---
<<dd_version: 2>>

These are the examples from the end of the [help file](help.html), in the
same order, with their output. They use Stata's `nlsw88` data; every line can
be pasted into Stata as is.

## Fit and store the models, then compare marginal effects

Factor syntax is required for the regression models; it is optional for
`mecompare`.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
sysuse nlsw88, clear

logit union i.married age i.race hours i.collgrad, vce(robust)
est store basemod

logit union i.married age i.race hours i.collgrad wage, vce(robust)
est store medmod

mecompare age collgrad race hours, models(basemod medmod)
<</dd_do>>
```

## Amount of change for continuous variables

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare age collgrad race hours, models(basemod medmod) amount(sd)
mecompare age collgrad race hours, models(basemod medmod) amount(sd 10)
<</dd_do>>
```

`amount(rate)` gives the instantaneous rate of change; `amount(dydx)` and
`amount(slope)` are synonyms.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare age hours, models(basemod medmod) amount(rate)
mecompare age hours, models(basemod medmod) amount(range)
<</dd_do>>
```

## Labeling the models

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare age collgrad race hours, models(basemod medmod) mod1name(Base Model) mod2name(Mediation Model)
<</dd_do>>
```

## Effects within levels of a variable (by, over)

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare age race, models(basemod medmod) over(collgrad)
mecompare age race, models(basemod medmod) by(collgrad)
mecompare age race, models(basemod medmod) by(collgrad married)
<</dd_do>>
```

Whether an effect differs across the levels (a test of interaction), jointly
and for one pair:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare age, models(basemod) by(race)
metest 1 = 2 = 3
metest 1 - 2
<</dd_do>>
```

For a nominal variable, one equality per contrast:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare race, models(basemod) by(collgrad)
metest (1 = 2) (3 = 4)
<</dd_do>>
```

## Values of the focal variables and covariates, including lists of values

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare age race, models(basemod medmod) atmeans
mecompare age, models(basemod) start(age=(35 40 45))
mecompare age, models(basemod) start(age=35) end(age=40)
mecompare age, models(basemod) start(age=(35 40)) end(age=(40 45))
mecompare age race, models(basemod medmod) covariates(hours=(20 40 60))
<</dd_do>>
```

## Summary measures for nominal variables

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare race, models(basemod medmod) pwcompare
mecompare race, models(basemod) meineq(weighted)
mecompare race, models(basemod medmod) meineq(all)
<</dd_do>>
```

## Total ME, which sums effects across outcome categories

For example, with an ordinal outcome:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
egen hours_ord = cut(hours), at(0 30 40 50 81)
ologit hours_ord c.age i.married i.race, vce(robust)
mecompare age married race, totalme
<</dd_do>>
```

## Comparing models fit over distinct groups

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
logit union age hours i.collgrad if south==1, vce(robust)
est store msouth
logit union age hours i.collgrad if south==0, vce(robust)
est store mnonsouth

mecompare age hours collgrad, models(msouth mnonsouth) groups groupnames(South NonSouth)
<</dd_do>>
```

## Cross-family comparison (same number of predictions)

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
logit union i.married age i.race hours i.collgrad, vce(robust)
est store logitmod
regress union i.married age i.race hours i.collgrad, vce(robust)
est store lpmmod

mecompare age race, models(logitmod lpmmod)
<</dd_do>>
```

## Choosing the prediction

With one model, any prediction `margins` allows; a count model offers several.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
nbreg hours c.age i.collgrad i.race, vce(robust)
est store cntbase

mecompare age collgrad race, models(cntbase)
mecompare age collgrad race, models(cntbase) predict(n)
mecompare age collgrad race, models(cntbase) predict(ir)
mecompare age collgrad race, models(cntbase) predict(pr(0))
<</dd_do>>
```

With two or more models, any prediction returning one quantity per model:

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
nbreg hours c.age i.collgrad i.race i.married, vce(robust)
est store cntmed

mecompare age collgrad race, models(cntbase cntmed) predict(n)
<</dd_do>>
```

## Passing an option to margins, e.g. effects in percentage points

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
mecompare age race, models(basemod) marginsopt(expression(100*predict(pr)))
<</dd_do>>
```

## Four nested models and custom comparisons with metest

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
use https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/gss_cme, clear
drop if year < 2000
drop if employed != 1
drop if missing(vhappy, college, wages, occprest, age, married, parent, woman, conserv, reltrad)

logit vhappy i.college, vce(robust)
estimates store m1
logit vhappy i.college i.married i.parent i.woman i.conserv i.reltrad i.year c.age##c.age, vce(robust)
estimates store m2
logit vhappy i.college c.wages i.married i.parent i.woman i.conserv i.reltrad i.year c.age##c.age, vce(robust)
estimates store m3
logit vhappy i.college c.wages c.occprest i.married i.parent i.woman i.conserv i.reltrad i.year c.age##c.age, vce(robust)
estimates store m4

mecompare college, models(m1 m2 m3 m4)
<</dd_do>>
```

Use `metest` to calculate the cross-model tests. Here, whether the effect
diminishes in each subsequent model.

```{.stata-run}
<<dd_do>>
metest 1 - 2
metest 2 - 3, add
metest 3 - 4, add
<</dd_do>>
```
